hook: Engineers are carving two massive caverns 50 metres beneath Sydney for a $7.4 billion tunnel.

sections.voiceover: Engineers are carving two massive caverns 50 metres beneath Sydney for a $7.4 billion tunnel.
sections.visual_cue: Wide aerial shot of Sydney Harbour transitioning to a subsurface cutaway diagram showing the tunnel depth.
b_roll: Subsurface engineering diagram of tunnel depth

sections.voiceover: Crews at Birchgrove excavated launch chambers measuring 120 metres long to house equipment. How do they fit 4400-tonne machines here?
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of industrial blueprints overlaid on the Birchgrove site.
b_roll: Engineering floor plans of launch chambers

sections.voiceover: Except these machines are even heavier, with the Barangaroo TBM weighing 4350 tonnes.
sections.visual_cue: Scale comparison graphic showing the TBM next to a standard skyscraper floor.

sections.voiceover: Specialized roadheaders carved the rock 44.7 metres below the surface to begin the drive. Each boring machine clears a 15.7-metre path.
sections.visual_cue: Animation of the roadheader cutting through sandstone.

sections.voiceover: Two 4400-tonne giants are now drilling the 6.5-kilometre tunnel.
sections.visual_cue: Final shot of the TBM rotating in the dark cavern.
